newsitem.title: UK: EU seen awarding up to 70,000 T sugar at tender.
newsitem.headline: EU seen awarding up to 70,000 T sugar at tender.

text.p: The European Union (EU) is expected to award up to 70,000 tonnes of current series white sugar at its weekly tender later on Wednesday, traders said.
Although the EU is lagging behind in its cumulative exports programme, traders said this week's tonnage award was unlikely to be vastly higher than the 44,500 tonnes awarded last week.
"I wouldn't expect a crazy scramble for licences," said one, estimating a range between 40,000 and 50,000 tonnes.
Another trader forecast a wider range between 40,000 and 70,000 tonnes.
"I think it will be a little bit more than last week but not all that much, judging by the volume of hedging you could identify yesterday," he said.
"I don't expect them to catch up this week or next week," he said, referring to the cumulative tonnage awarded in sugar export licences in the 1996/97 tender series.
The interest in restitution licences was likely to pick up from February, he added.
This week's maximum restitution for export licences was forecast at 45.296 Ecus (European currency units) per 100 kg of sugar, based on the Paris March white sugar contract.
Last week's maximum restitution level was 45.902 Ecus.
